editorial:
Ever wonder how much money actually controls your life? You get to see ten different takes on that question here. Since this is an anthology, you aren't following one single story. Instead, you get ten quick snapshots of people in South Korea dealing with cash, greed, and desperation. Some stories are funny, while others feel a bit heavier, but they all share that same nervous energy. It feels like a collection of short stories where every character is just one bad decision away from losing everything or hitting the jackpot.

What really works here is the variety. You won't get bored because if one story doesn't click with you, a new one starts in a few minutes. The acting feels very real and grounded, making the twists hit harder. While some shorts are a bit too brief to fully dive into the characters, the fast pacing keeps you hooked.
endingExplained: Because this is a collection of short films, there isn't one single ending. Each story wraps up its own lesson about money. Some characters find a way to get rich through tricks, while others end up empty-handed. The final segments show that no matter how much money people chase, it usually brings more stress than happiness. The movie ends by leaving you to think about your own relationship with cash and greed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves short stories and social dramas.
